front_blocks.md: What is the purpose of the CPU?

back_blocks.md: The purpose of the Central Processing Unit is to **execute instructions**, which it achieves by completing **processor cycles**.

cards.front_md: What is the purpose of the CPU?
cards.back_md: The purpose of the Central Processing Unit is to **execute instructions**, which it achieves by completing **processor cycles**.

front_blocks.md: Name the three stages of the processor cycle.

cards.front_md: Name the three stages of the processor cycle.

front_blocks.md: What happens during the fetch stage of the processor cycle?

back_blocks.md: The next instruction or data is **fetched from the computer's memory (RAM)** and brought back to the CPU.

cards.front_md: What happens during the fetch stage of the processor cycle?
cards.back_md: The next instruction or data is **fetched from the computer's memory (RAM)** and brought back to the CPU.

front_blocks.md: What happens during the decode stage of the processor cycle?

back_blocks.md: The CPU **works out what is required** from the instruction.

cards.front_md: What happens during the decode stage of the processor cycle?
cards.back_md: The CPU **works out what is required** from the instruction.

front_blocks.md: Give two things the CPU might do during the execute stage.

back_blocks.md: The CPU **carries out the instruction**, which could mean **performing a calculation**, **storing a result back in main memory**, or **fetching data from a different location** in main memory.

cards.front_md: Give two things the CPU might do during the execute stage.
cards.back_md: The CPU **carries out the instruction**, which could mean **performing a calculation**, **storing a result back in main memory**, or **fetching data from a different location** in main memory.

back_blocks.md: Clock speed is the measure of a processor's speed, giving the **number of processor cycles that can take place in 1 second**.

cards.back_md: Clock speed is the measure of a processor's speed, giving the **number of processor cycles that can take place in 1 second**.

front_blocks.md: How many instructions per second can a clock speed of 3.5 GHz perform?

back_blocks.md: A clock speed of 3.5 GHz can perform up to **3.5 billion instructions per second**, because a gigahertz means a billion cycles per second.

cards.front_md: How many instructions per second can a clock speed of 3.5 GHz perform?
cards.back_md: A clock speed of 3.5 GHz can perform up to **3.5 billion instructions per second**, because a gigahertz means a billion cycles per second.

back_blocks.md: A core **works like it is its own CPU**, so a multi-core processor has **multiple separate processing units** that can fetch, decode and execute instructions at the same time.

cards.back_md: A core **works like it is its own CPU**, so a multi-core processor has **multiple separate processing units** that can fetch, decode and execute instructions at the same time.

front_blocks.md: How many instructions per second can a quad-core CPU running at 3 GHz perform?

back_blocks.md: 4 cores × 3 GHz gives **12 billion instructions per second**.

cards.front_md: How many instructions per second can a quad-core CPU running at 3 GHz perform?
cards.back_md: 4 cores × 3 GHz gives **12 billion instructions per second**.

front_blocks.md: A slower clock speed allows more instructions to be fetched and executed per second.

back_blocks.md: The **faster** the clock speed, the **more instructions** can be fetched and executed per second.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A slower clock speed allows more instructions to be fetched and executed per second.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

The **faster** the clock speed, the **more instructions** can be fetched and executed per second.

front_blocks.md: How does a faster processor improve a user's experience when playing a game?

back_blocks.md: A faster processor **fetches, decodes and executes more instructions per second**, so **graphics render more quickly and at greater resolution**, making the visuals **smoother** and the environment **more realistic**, and allowing **more actions** to be carried out.
